title: Buzz and Traycer core-source research for LVX Agent Studio
method: GitHub connector metadata followed by complete shallow source checkouts, pinned before inspection. Static source research only: no installs, external repository scripts, provider sessions, credentials, user chats or memory vaults were used.

evidence.observation: Rust relay is source of truth; authenticated, signed events are persisted and fanned out. ACP harness is a separate bridge from mentions to subprocess agents.

Documented Codex/Claude integrations are ACP adapters; Codex instructions explicitly request OPENAI_API_KEY rather than a ChatGPT subscription, and Claude example uses ANTHROPIC_API_KEY. This is evidence about this pinned integration, not current upstream provider policy.
One resolved scope keys context/session/queue state; thread policy uses canonical roots, DMs remain conversation-scoped. Channel is still the default and authorization boundary.
Successful-delivery state belongs to the provider session. Session affinity and generations stop busy-owner duplicate sessions and stale workers from reusing invalid context.
Queue caps are 500 per scope and per channel, batches 50, retries 10 with bounded exponential backoff; overflow drops events and retry exhaustion returns a dead-letter batch to caller.
Context is fetched for the resolved thread/DM target, filtered by exact delivered ids, and hydration/delivery state commits after protocol success. Token/request limits trigger session rotation.
Standing instruction bodies are preserved verbatim for review parity; untrusted values embedded into semantic framing need delimiter escaping.
Structured raw and semantic events carry sequence, timestamp, worker, channel, session and turn identity. Replay is process-local and capped at 1000, not durable history.

Subprocess stdio and visible stderr, Windows no-console launch, session IDs, JSON-RPC unknown-method replies and cleanup state are explicit. Permission requests automatically select allow_once when available; that policy should not be copied blindly.

Writer ownership returns only after a complete flushed NDJSON frame; aborted/failed partial writes close the transport rather than letting a subsequent frame corrupt the stream. Source includes negative regression tests, not executed in this research.

Fresh process/session is bounded by cancellation and deadline with shutdown. Refusal, max_tokens and max_turn_requests are represented as Completed reasons, which is transport completion rather than task acceptance.

Ordered workflows support conditions, timeouts and approval suspension; executor explicitly delegates durable approval recording/resumption to caller and still has a persistence TODO. A schema or suspended token alone does not prove a complete approval flow.

Quality comes partly from instructions: work visibly, inspect actual files, preserve exact-state evidence, validate, obtain a fresh review and respect repository guidance. These are behavioral guidance, not enforced acceptance gates.

Inbound author policy defaults owner-only and can fail closed without a resolved owner; cancellation/rotation are resolved by scope. Direct peer communication requires deliberate sender policy rather than assuming membership is sufficient.
Root project license is Apache-2.0; retain applicable attribution/license/notice material for any actual reuse and inspect third-party dependencies separately.
Repository contains clients, CLI and protocol; Host and cloud backends are absent. Electron shell, React GUI, shared transport and versioned protocol are public.
Per-method major/minor protocol versioning is negotiated; CLI downloads a signed host. Production cloud/runtime reproduction is outside the public source checkout.

GUI drives SDK/JSON-RPC; TUI is a real PTY. Terminal Claude/Codex/OpenCode can use A2A tools, but only Claude terminal has inbound delivery; GUI agents have both. Gemini is absent from the inspected GUI and TUI roster.
Explicit regression matrix corroborates Codex/OpenCode TUI receive=false and Claude TUI receive=true; unknown terminal harness gets neither capability. Tests were inspected, not run.

List entries expose locality, transcript/send capabilities, cwd/worktree and activity. A2A enqueue is fire-and-forget with broker responseId for reply correlation; cross-host delivery is rejected. Transcript retrieval is structured provider history, with no raw PTY fallback.

Stable Studio artifact and resumable provider session IDs are separate. Codex provider ID can arrive asynchronously via thread/started. Launch carries profile, cwd and busy worktree paths; Claude session-id drift is separately recorded.

Versioned durable inbox uses eventId and ack after surfacing; older monitors get weaker server-side compatibility ack. Full bodies can be retrieved in bounded pages when monitor output truncates. Public code defines contract, not hidden host storage implementation.
Message envelope identifies sender, provider and reply requirement; reply uses the sender-thread responseId and terminal output points to full inbox when cut off.

Graph log contract describes append-only SQLite rows and cursor resume; separate A2A message, stalled notice and agent-created facts with jumpable chat/terminal origins. Unknown unrepresentable kinds may be skipped; snapshot frame is batching, not proof of catch-up.

Display projection preserves raw event history, aggregates one unordered edge per pair and derives open reply state causally. Parent lineage is layout only, not fake communication. Wall-clock display sort is distinct from causal ordering.

Real ReactFlow graph renders agent nodes and A2A edges at a playback cursor, with pair/agent details, transport health and jumps to original chats. This is a useful presentation model independent of its host implementation.

Per-host subscriptions retain event arrays/cursors across UI detach; generation fences ignore stale callbacks, retries are bounded and unreachable differs from connecting. Renderer mounting does not own session lifetime.

Catalog exposes surface, availability, API-key requirement and supported permission modes; plan fetch returns source, status, contentHash and missing-blob state. Protocol claims host rejects unsupported permission mode, but hidden runtime cannot be independently inspected.

Run settings are fixed as a complete tuple on send; model/harness cannot late-bind during an accepted turn. Queue has edit/cancel/reorder/steer and explicit handling of safe-point vs interrupt-restart.

Presentation records preserve unknown provider IDs as generic labels; opaque hostPrivate anchors are excluded from presentation validation. Readable conversation history is not identical to resumable provider state.
Electron uses contextIsolation=true, nodeIntegration=false and sandbox=true; OS work stays behind main/preload IPC.

README claims subscriptions, shared context and direct provider requests but qualifies A2A by runtime; release builds may enable analytics/crash reporting. Claims about hidden host context transformation are not source-verifiable here.
MIT license applies to the public checkout, with copyright/permission notice retention. It does not establish rights to unavailable Host/cloud source or trademark assets.

findings.title: Different cores, complementary lessons
findings.assessment: Buzz is a full Rust collaboration relay plus ACP execution service; Traycer exposes a rich client/protocol and visual graph but not its Host. Borrow local event/session patterns rather than introducing either entire platform into Electron/CJS.

findings.title: Buzz does not prove native subscription execution
findings.assessment: Its documented Codex/Claude ACP examples use API keys. No successful local subscription execution was tested, so retain native CLI login and implement provider adapters independently.

findings.title: Traycer A2A is asymmetric at the terminal boundary
findings.assessment: A tool-enabled Codex terminal is not necessarily a message receiver. Discovery, outbound send, inbound idle continuation and mid-turn steering must be separately represented and tested; Gemini support is not established by the inspected roster.

findings.title: Agent identity and provider session identity must remain separate
findings.assessment: A canvas node can outlive a process, while a provider may allocate or change its native resume ID asynchronously. Persist workspace, node, provider, provider session, generation and actual cwd; never infer them from current UI selection.

findings.title: Exact context delivery improves quality without flattening native sessions
findings.assessment: Avoid repeatedly injecting full transcripts or a global summary. Preserve native provider context and full original assistant messages; add only explicitly routed peer messages, with provenance and exact delivery state. Presentation history alone cannot reconstruct opaque provider context.

findings.title: Concurrency needs ownership and stale-result fences
findings.assessment: One active turn per agent/provider session, worker ownership, generation-tagged callbacks and atomic queue transitions prevent duplicate continuation, stale writes after cancellation and node remounts restarting work.

findings.title: Retry and overflow policy are user-visible correctness concerns
findings.assessment: Bounded retries and cancellation-safe framing are valuable, but Buzz queue overflow drops should not become silent Studio message loss. Persist admission before dispatch, reject/backpressure at limits and display blocked/dead-letter state. Durable at-least-once needs idempotent consumption; it is not semantic exactly-once execution.

findings.title: Visible chat needs durable events beyond live stdout
findings.assessment: Buzz observer replay is bounded RAM. Use workspace-scoped append-only durable Studio events and resumable renderer cursors; retain full raw and parsed output, original peer text and source links, while acknowledging adapter/provider consumption separately from enqueue.

findings.title: Graph edges must show actual communication, not organizational fiction
findings.assessment: Traycer preserves full message log and derives aggregated pair edges, unanswered requests and playback. Keep desired workflow/dependency edges visually distinct from observed messages and parent lineage; every communication edge should open its exact messages.

findings.title: Transport completion is not quality acceptance
findings.assessment: Buzz isolated task Completed includes refusal and token limits; review instructions and plan schemas are not enforced acceptance. LVX needs independent transport, semantic outcome and review/check acceptance fields, with artifacts/check results linked to the exact work state.

findings.title: Preserve explicit native permission policy
findings.assessment: Buzz auto-approves allow_once ACP requests. Adapt session lifecycle, not this blanket permission policy or generated provider config. Provider permissions and pending approval should be visible on the node; renderer remains isolated from process execution.

findings.title: Model/provider switches cannot promise identical native context
findings.assessment: Traycer markets shared context but Host transformation is unavailable. Public protocol fixes model/effort/harness tuple per accepted send and distinguishes opaque session anchors. A Studio switch should create an explicit handoff/fork with preserved history and disclosed context boundary, not overwrite a running session identity.

findings.title: Direct collaboration needs admitted routing and loop controls
findings.assessment: Buzz owner-only default would reject ordinary peer authors unless configured; Traycer correlates expected replies by sender thread. Explicit directed subscriptions, full-message envelopes, reply ids, deduplication, bounded auto-hops and pause/stop controls enable direct peers without an opaque central prompt writer.

findings.title: Cross-device visibility is not cross-host deliverability
findings.assessment: Traycer can enumerate or render agents across hosts yet rejects cross-host A2A at this contract. Studio should initially scope execution/routing to one validated workspace host and expose unavailable capabilities rather than implying federation.

findings.title: Open licenses do not make all advertised runtime reproducible
findings.assessment: Buzz root license is Apache-2.0; Traycer public code is MIT. Host/cloud internals and provider subscription rules are separate. Source reuse needs proper notice preservation, and third-party assets/dependencies need their own review.

recommendations.action: Implement native CLI adapter boundaries in Electron main/CJS: discover, version/probe, launch turn, resume, cancel and parse provider output. Keep existing native login, native permission settings and original output; use argv arrays without shell interpolation or provider config mutation.
recommendations.acceptance: Each supported provider can execute and resume a small genuine turn using its native session ID; unsupported/login/permission failures appear as blockers and never fall back silently to API billing.

recommendations.action: Persist node and session separately with workspaceId, agentId, provider, nativeSessionId, generation, cwd, argv/settings and capability snapshot. Serialize turns per session and fence late events after stop/restart.
recommendations.acceptance: Concurrent enqueue produces one active turn; changing selected nodes or reopening the view cannot redirect messages or spawn a duplicate provider session.

recommendations.action: Use a durable local SQLite outbox/inbox and append-only event stream. Track admitted, queued, started, provider-completed, blocked and failed separately from task/review acceptance; acknowledge once the adapter has actually accepted the delivery, with deduplication keys and explicit unknown-outcome recovery.
recommendations.acceptance: Restart before dispatch, after native acceptance and after result persistence preserves original messages and honest state; no ambiguous non-idempotent turn is automatically retried as if nothing happened.

recommendations.action: Deliver full original assistant text directly along enabled peer links after the recipient becomes idle. Preserve source event/agent/provider identity and correlation outside the original text; no hidden summarizer, role rewrite or forced planning prefix. Enforce loop budget and user pause/stop.
recommendations.acceptance: Sender and receiver panes show matching payload hashes, source origin and exact delivery status; a two-agent cycle reaches its configured boundary and remains manually continuable.

recommendations.action: Make graph nodes live session views with provider, cwd, availability, current turn, permissions and open chat. Distinguish configured routes/dependencies from observed communication; aggregate observed pairs only for presentation and open full chronological messages on click.
recommendations.acceptance: Every observed edge has real event evidence; selecting it opens original bodies and status without inventing delivery from an enabled route.

recommendations.action: Expose per-provider capabilities for native resume, structured output, idle continuation, unsolicited/mid-turn delivery, transcript retrieval and permission interaction. Probe rather than assume equality; make unsupported Gemini/native modes explicit until verified.
recommendations.acceptance: An adapter lacking inbound steering can still receive a queued next native turn, but the UI never reports that message as injected into a currently running turn.

recommendations.action: Attach human-visible plans, checks and independent review as optional explicit artifacts and reviewer nodes. Store command/exit/result/work-state evidence and a separate acceptance decision rather than relabeling every provider exit as done.
recommendations.acceptance: Refusal, limit, cancellation, permission pause and failed checks remain distinct; a reviewer can inspect original context/artifacts and deliver feedback directly without an orchestrator rewriting it.

recommendations.action: Treat model/provider change as explicit new-turn configuration or handoff/fork. Preserve the original native session and full conversation; show which native state is resumable and what was carried as plain messages.
recommendations.acceptance: Switching models during a running turn cannot silently alter that turn or claim opaque hidden context was migrated.

recommendations.action: Keep a narrow contextBridge/preload API and main-owned process registry. Validate workspace/path/node bindings on every mutation, use explicit argv, retain provider stderr separately and close a transport after partial-frame failure.
recommendations.acceptance: Malformed renderer requests and stale generations cannot target arbitrary processes; cancellation and shutdown terminate the intended child tree on Windows without corrupting the next session.

recommendations.action: Reuse concepts first. If source is copied, record exact pinned provenance and carry required license/notice material; avoid importing relay/cloud, analytics, unavailable Host binaries or provider branding just to get a graph.
recommendations.acceptance: The Studio works locally with the installed native CLIs and its own persistence; source attribution matches the material actually reused.

fourPassReview.name: Complete implementation of research
fourPassReview.result: Inspected both complete source trees; traced relay/ACP/session/queue/context/observer and Traycer protocol/terminal/graph/client boundaries; pinned commits and recorded evidence.

fourPassReview.name: Expert reread
fourPassReview.result: Separated GUI SDK sessions from native interactive TUI, source-verifiable implementations from hidden Host contracts, transport success from task quality, and bounded observer buffers from durable storage.

fourPassReview.name: Refutation and failure audit
fourPassReview.result: Rejected universal subscription/A2A/context-migration claims using API-key documentation, explicit terminal capability predicates and tests, hidden Host boundary, queue overflow, auto-approval, refusal/limit completion and graph representability exceptions.

fourPassReview.name: Polish and evidence audit
fourPassReview.result: Added scoped negative claims, concrete Electron/CJS adaptation, exact provenance, limitations, actionable acceptance scenarios and paired Markdown narrative; all cited path/ranges checked against pinned checkout.

limitations: Static inspection only; upstream tests were not installed or run and subscription CLI behavior was not exercised.

Traycer Host, model/context conversion, durable inbox storage, permission enforcement and cloud backend implementation are absent from this public repository; their public contracts are not independent implementation proof.
Buzz ACP README can lag external adapter releases; conclusions are limited to the pinned source integration, not current external authentication entitlements.
No general Gemini native subscription integration is established by these inspected source surfaces.
Source licenses were inventoried; this report does not assess every transitive dependency, third-party asset or provider service term.
